bio: Paul Richard LePage (; born October 9, 1948) is an American businessman and politician who served as the 74th governor of Maine from 2011 to 2019. A member of the Republican Party, he also served as the mayor of Waterville, Maine, from 2004 to 2011.

items.t: Supports eliminating Maine's income tax, and proposed a constitutional amendment to do so.
items.q: LePage advocates eliminating Maine's income tax, believing it to be an impediment to economic growth for the state.

items.t: Supported a 5% flat tax on all households earning more than $30,000.
items.q: He opposed raising any taxes during his term as governor and supported the creation of a 5% flat tax on all households earning more than $30,000.

items.t: Vetoed at least one bill raising Maine's minimum wage.
items.q: LePage has vetoed at least one bill for increasing Maine's minimum wage

items.t: Supported a competing proposal to raise Maine's minimum wage to $10 an hour instead of the $12 referendum.
items.q: he stated that he supported a competing proposal to raise it to $10 an hour as less harmful to businesses

items.t: Proposed allowing businesses to pay child workers a training wage of $5.25 an hour.
items.q: LePage has proposed allowing businesses to pay child workers a training wage of $5.25 an hour

items.t: Is against offering a home for asylum seekers in Maine.
items.q: Governor LePage is opposed to offering a home for asylum seekers in Maine.

items.t: Appeared at the annual Hands Around the Capitol pro-life rally at the Maine State House, beginning in 2011.
items.q: He has appeared at the annual anti-abortion Hands Around the Capitol rally at the Maine State House, first doing so at the 2011 event.

items.t: Said he hoped to repeal Maine's ban on Bisphenol A (BPA); the ban became law without his signature.
items.q: LePage refused to sign the bill, but it became law without his signature.

items.t: Supported increased use of fossil fuels, vetoed clean energy bills, and promoted offshore drilling.
items.q: LePage supported increased use of fossil fuels, vetoed clean energy bills, sought to eliminate environmental regulations, was the lone Atlantic coast governor to promote offshore drilling

items.t: Criticized wind power and Maine's 2008 Wind Energy Act expansion of installed capacity.
items.q: LePage has criticized wind power and in particular the large-scale expansion of installed capacity mandated by Maine's 2008 Wind Energy Act

items.t: Supports shallow-water offshore drilling in Maine waters, but not deep-water drilling.
items.q: He has said he would support shallow-water offshore drilling in Maine waters, but not deep-water drilling

items.t: Proposed zoning 10 million acres of northern Maine for development and repealing laws requiring manufacturers to take back recyclable goods.
items.q: LePage proposed zoning 10 million acres (40,000 km 2 ) of northern Maine for development, repealing laws that require manufacturers to take back recyclable goods for disposal

items.t: Supported a school voucher system and pay structured to reward teachers for performance.
items.q: LePage supported a school voucher system and structuring pay to reward teachers for performance.

items.t: Signed a bill aligning Maine with the Common Core State Standards Initiative (2011), then opposed the standards and barred their federal implementation by executive order (2013).
items.q: On September 4, he issued an executive order prohibiting the Maine Department of Education from implementing any federal education standards

items.t: Proposed allowing public funds to go to religious schools; the Maine Supreme Judicial Court found the proposal unconstitutional.
items.q: LePage made a proposal to allow public funds to go to religious schools; the proposal was found unconstitutional by the Maine Supreme Judicial Court.

items.t: Supports the death penalty for the murder of a baby and for drug dealers whose drugs cause a fatal overdose.
items.q: LePage supports the death penalty in cases of the murder of a baby.

items.t: Issued 236 pardons to 115 people while governor.
items.q: While governor, LePage issued 236 pardons to 115 people.

items.t: Is against Maine's Clean Elections Act and proposed eliminating all its funding in his 2014–2015 budget.
items.q: LePage is opposed to the Maine Clean Elections Act, which provides funding for publicly-financed campaigns in Maine

items.t: Was against changing Maine's voting system from plurality voting to ranked choice voting.
items.q: LePage was opposed to efforts to change Maine's voting system from plurality voting to ranked choice voting

items.t: Supports requiring petition signatures to be gathered in each Maine county and a greater total number of signatures to qualify an issue for the ballot.
items.q: He has expressed support for requiring petition signatures to be gathered in each Maine county

items.t: Was against allowing same-sex couples to marry in 2009 and supports state recognition of civil unions for all couples.
items.q: In 2009, LePage opposed allowing same-sex couples to marry. He does support the state recognizing only civil unions of all couples

items.t: Vetoed a bill banning conversion therapy in 2018.
items.q: In 2018, LePage vetoed a bill banning conversion therapy

items.t: Pledged to oppose legislation for transgender students in grades K–12.
items.q: LePage then pledged to oppose legislation for transgender students

items.t: Is against expanding casino gambling in Maine.
items.q: LePage opposes the expansion of casino gambling in Maine

items.t: Proposed allowing children aged 12 and up to work and a $5.25 subminimum wage, rolling back child labor laws.
items.q: As governor, LePage attempted to roll back child labor laws, proposing a $5.25 subminimum wage.

items.t: Removed a mural depicting the history of Maine's labor movement from the Department of Labor lobby.
items.q: Despite protests, on March 28 it was disclosed that the murals had been removed over the weekend.

items.t: Called for abolishing term limits for Maine legislators.
items.q: He has called for the abolition of term limits for Maine legislators, who are limited to four consecutive two-year terms

items.t: Said the size of state government is likely too large and would probably seek to reduce the number of state employees.
items.q: LePage has stated that the size of state government is likely too large and that he would probably seek to reduce the number of state employees.

items.t: Issued 642 vetoes as governor, more than all his predecessors since 1917 combined.
items.q: LePage issued 642 vetoes, which broke the record of 118 set by Governor James B. Longley and was more than all his predecessors since 1917 combined.

items.t: Supports removing children of welfare recipients from their homes if the recipients use illegal drugs and refuse rehab.
items.q: LePage supports the idea of the state removing the children of welfare recipients from their homes if the recipients are found to be using illegal drugs and refuse to enter rehab.

items.t: Vetoed a bill to establish retail cannabis sales in Maine in 2018.
items.q: in 2018 he vetoed a bill to establish retail sales of cannabis in Maine in accordance with an initiative that voters approved in 2016.

items.t: Called for additional Maine DEA agents, judges and prosecutors, and for drug traffickers to be held in "super-max" facilities.
items.q: LePage has called for additional Maine DEA agents, judges, and prosecutors to fight drugs.
